question: What are all the powers and functions of the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)? Include its nature, parent legislation, and ministry.
cardAnswer: NTCA is a statutory authority established under the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2006, under MoEFCC. Its functions are: (1) Approve Tiger Conservation Plans made by State Governments (states make the plans; NTCA only approves). (2) Evaluate and assess sustainable ecology; prohibit ecologically unsustainable land use such as mining and industry in tiger reserves. (3) Establish standards and norms for tiger tourism in both core and buffer zones. (4) Gather data for conservation — disease surveillance, mortality surveys, patrolling reports. (5) Approve use of tiger reserves or connecting areas for non-tiger purposes in public interest, but this requires NBWL approval — not NTCA alone. (6) Extend tiger reserve management to adjacent areas through eco-development. (7) Capacity building for tiger reserve officers and staff.

question: Describe the complete methodology of the All India Tiger Estimation (AITE) — frequency, conducting bodies, all four phases with tools used, and the status of each technique.
cardAnswer: AITE is conducted every 4 years since 2006, jointly by NTCA and WII (Wildlife Institute of India) with state forest departments. The four phases are: Phase I — M-STrIPES App (Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status): field data on signs, sightings, and human impact collected digitally; mandatory and primary for ground evidence. Phase II — Remote Sensing & GIS: habitat characterisation, vegetation indices, and land-use changes analysed via satellite imagery. Phase III — Camera Trapping & SECR: individual tigers identified by unique stripe patterns using ExtractCompare software; Spatially Explicit Capture-Recapture (SECR) models estimate population density; this is the gold standard for population figures. Phase IV — Intensive Annual Monitoring at tiger reserve level to track survival and recruitment between 4-year national cycles, using 25 cameras per 100 sq km and distance sampling for prey. DNA profiling of scat/hair is a supplementary/verification method, especially in low-density or high-canopy areas like Northeast India. Pugmark Census is now obsolete for counting — used only as a presence/absence index; population numbers are never derived from pugmarks.

question: Describe the complete vulture drug ban situation — primary cause of death, all banned drugs with dates, the Aceclofenac mechanism trap, drugs under surveillance, and safe alternatives.

question: Describe the complete dolphin conservation picture in India — all dolphin categories and species found, WPA protection, the four global freshwater dolphin species with scientific names and status, the Gangetic Dolphin's special designation, population, threats, and NMCG's role.
cardAnswer: India has four dolphin categories: Freshwater — Gangetic/Ganges River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica) found in the Ganges-Brahmaputra system and its tributaries across India, Nepal, and Bangladesh, and also in the Karnaphuli-Sangu river systems; Freshwater — Indus River Dolphin found in Punjab (Indus River); Brackish water — Irrawaddy Dolphins in Odisha's brackish waters; Marine — 15 species along Indian coasts. All cetaceans (dolphins) are protected under Schedule I of WPA 1972, the highest degree of protection. The Gangetic Dolphin is India's National Aquatic Animal (declared by MoEF). Its population is approximately 2,000. The four global freshwater dolphin species are: Gangetic Dolphin (Platanista gangetica, Ganges-Brahmaputra, India/Nepal/Bangladesh, Endangered); Baiji (Lipotes vexillifer, Yangtze, China, functionally extinct since 2006 — NOT 2010); Bhulan (Platanista minor, Indus, Pakistan, Endangered); Boto (Inia geoffrensis, Amazon, Latin America, Endangered). Threats to Gangetic Dolphins: pollution, entanglement in fishing nets, poaching, and population fragmentation due to dam construction. NMCG (National Mission for Clean Ganga) launched a dolphin conservation programme in 2016.

question: Describe Project Cheetah completely — its global significance, launch details, location, source countries with numbers, species reintroduced with scientific names, administering bodies, and key traps.
cardAnswer: Project Cheetah is the first inter-continental translocation of a large carnivore in global history. It was launched on September 17, 2022, at Kuno National Park in Madhya Pradesh (not Rajasthan — Gandhi Sagar was an earlier candidate but was not selected). Source countries: Namibia contributed 8 cheetahs initially (2022); South Africa contributed 12 cheetahs in 2023. The species reintroduced is the African Cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) — NOT the Asiatic Cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus venaticus), which is critically endangered and found only in Iran. Project Cheetah is administered by MoEFCC, NTCA, and WII. Wild-born cubs were born from 2023 onwards.
